title: Layer eviction and a lock around a plain cache

blocks.text: The page builds a cache from layers, each knowing one thing:
`SimpleCache` stores and is **not** thread-safe; composing it with more parts does not change that. `Cache` and `SimpleCache` are given. Write the other two layers in `Caches`:

items: `BoundedCache(delegate, maxSize)` adds least-recently-used eviction over any cache. It does not need to be thread-safe on its own: `ThreadSafeCache` provides that when it wraps it. With `maxSize` 2, putting `a`, `b`, `c` evicts `a`;
reading a key with `get` makes it the most recently used: put `a`, `b`, read `a`, put `c`, and `b` is evicted. Reading a key that is not there changes nothing;
a removed key is gone from the eviction order too: put `a`, `b`, remove `a`, then put `c`, `d`, `e`, and the cache holds exactly `d` and `e`;
writing a key that is already there evicts nothing and also makes it the most recently used: put `a`, `b`, put `a` again, put `c`, and `b` is evicted;

`ThreadSafeCache(delegate)` is **the one synchronizing layer**: every call it forwards holds one lock, so while one call is inside the wrapped cache, any other call (`get`, `put`, `remove`, `size` or `containsKey`) waits.

cases.says: A bounded cache of 2 evicts a when c is added, and the thread-safe wrapper forwards every call.
After get(a), adding c to the full cache evicts b, not a.
Writing a again evicts nothing, and then adding c evicts b, not a.
With room for 2: put a and b, remove a, put c, d and e, and the cache holds exactly d and e.
While a put is inside the wrapped cache, a get, remove, size or containsKey through ThreadSafeCache waits and never runs alongside it.

concepts: Eviction is another decorator, BoundedCache, layered over any cache without synchronization of its own.
Composing parts that are not thread-safe does not make the whole thread-safe; an explicit synchronizing wrapper does.
Synchronization lives in one wrapper, ThreadSafeCache, around a cache that has none, so where the lock is can be read off one class.
